The July 2025 timing and claimed catastrophic new backlog are contradicted by Social Security Administration performance releases. corrected_draft.description_long: On July 23, 2025, the Social Security Administration reported that its initial disability claims backlog had fallen to 940,000 pending cases. SSA said this was a 25 percent reduction from a record of more than 1.2 million cases the previous year. The agency attributed service changes to new telephone technology, process engineering and resource alignment. It also reported faster customer service: its National 800 Number handled nearly 1.3 million calls the prior week, 70 percent more than in the comparable week a year earlier, while the average wait to speak with an agent was six minutes. SSA said field office wait times averaged 23 minutes so far that year, compared with 30 minutes in the prior year. The release further reported that the number of pending disability hearings remained at historic lows and average hearing waits had fallen by 60 days since June 2024. These are agency-reported service figures and do not establish the separate claim that millions newly faced crippling delays after July DOGE cuts. The narrow event supported here is SSA’s July 23 public report on service performance and backlog reduction.
